primary_sources.source: Republic Act No. 12009, New Government Procurement Act
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Sections 3, 7, 9-13, 20-25, 26-40, 67-68, 75-76, 81-83, and 112-117 establish proportionality and value for money; an approved APP; market scoping and lifecycle costing; PhilGEPS; fit-for-purpose modes including Competitive Dialogue, Unsolicited Offer with Bid Matching, and Direct Procurement for Science, Technology and Innovation; disclosure and liability rules for subcontractors; contract-performance monitoring; and a transition regime.

primary_sources.source: Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 12009, approved February 4, 2025 and published February 10, 2025
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Rule II operationalizes strategic procurement planning. Section 10.4 requires market scoping for the PPMP, including supplier capability, cost estimates, lifecycle cost, technical and functional requirements, and suitable procurement approaches. The mode-specific rules condition rather than guarantee access to innovation-oriented procurement.

Sections 3-8 cover interoperability, resilience, capacity, whole-of-government architecture and project governance; Section 6(a) directs DICT to adopt policy supporting startups and technology adoption; Sections 24-25 require risk-proportionate information security, periodic control testing, privacy by design/default, agency stewardship of master data and secure APIs; Section 26 permits private-sector contracts and partnerships subject to public accountability, transparency and good-governance rules; Sections 27-29 strengthen ICT training.

primary_sources.source: World Bank, GovTech Procurement Practice Note
primary_sources.type: Official international-government procurement guidance based on project practice
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Treats GovTech procurement as a lifecycle choice among SaaS, COTS and custom build; calls for realistic requirements, implementation capacity, change management, maintenance, data portability, ownership and exit planning; identifies lock-in, customization, skills-retention and fragmented-development risks.

primary_sources.source: Government of Canada, Right Cloud Selection Guidance
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Requires an exit strategy aligned with continuity needs and identifies bankruptcy, acquisition, price changes, retraining and switching costs as vendor-lock risks; recommends open standards, recompete capability and backup or disaster-recovery arrangements.

primary_sources.source: Venkatesh, Morris, Davis and Davis, User Acceptance of Information Technology: Toward a Unified View
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: UTAUT field data across four organizations found performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence and facilitating conditions predict behavioral intention or use, with relationships moderated by context. It supports measuring acceptance and enabling conditions, not equating intention with organizational purchase.

primary_sources.source: Talebi and Rezania, Value creation in public procurement of innovation: a case of engaging start-ups by a local government
primary_sources.relevant_provisions: Examines value creation through a local-government program engaging startups; its single-case, collaborative-process evidence can motivate mechanisms and questions but cannot establish that any particular startup product is viable or scalable.

evidence.legal_or_evidentiary_status: RA 12009 applies to LGU procurement and is binding, subject to its IRR and the stated transition provisions. An LGU purchase still requires an authorized need, budget and APP/PPMP alignment, an appropriate statutory mode, eligibility and evaluation, award authority, and contract management. Competitive Dialogue, Unsolicited Offer with Bid Matching, or an STI mode are legal possibilities only when their conditions are met; they are not startup preferences or entitlements. RA 12254 is also binding across covered government entities and supplies a policy basis for startup-supportive, interoperable and resilient e-government, but Sections 6 and 26 do not exempt a private provider from procurement, budgeting, accounting, auditing, privacy, security, records, or sectoral requirements. World Bank and foreign-government documents are advisory in the Philippines. UTAUT and the startup-engagement case study are empirical evidence, not legal mandates and not direct evidence about Zamboanga City or this product.
evidence.evidence_limits_and_conflicts: The laws establish authority, process and safeguards; they do not demonstrate demand, affordability, usability, operational improvement, disaster outcomes, or commercial sustainability for the proposed startup. An innovation-friendly procurement route can coexist with competition, documentary burden and long sales cycles. Staff statements of usefulness can be affected by courtesy, novelty or researcher presence and cannot substitute for signed authority, a funded APP line, procurement eligibility or an executed contract. A single-city prototype and purposive sample do not generalize to other LGUs, hazards or deployment scales. Lifecycle cost is locally dependent on hosting, security, support, data migration, integrations, training, connectivity and exit obligations. The World Bank guidance and foreign cloud guidance are transferable design references, not Philippine compliance authority. RA 12254 is recent; agency-specific implementation, implementing issuances and procurement transition practice should be checked again before production procurement.

chapter_one_integration.objective_revisions: Retain the paper's six operational submodules and make startup feasibility an evaluation dimension rather than inventing a seventh product module. User and Organization Management should test multi-organization onboarding, role assignment, administrator handover and separation of customer data. Disaster Reporting should test guided capture, drafts, timestamps and low-connectivity recovery. Verification should test status transitions, reviewer attribution, conflict notes and correction without claiming that software creates legal verification authority. SitRep Generation should test traceable compilation and export while leaving official approval and submission to authorized personnel. Catalog should test controlled reference-data maintenance and versioning. Dashboard should test filterable operational summaries with drill-down to source records. Evaluation should measure task completion, accuracy, time, usability, intention to use, facilitating conditions, administrator workload, support needs and procurement readiness separately. The student prototype may demonstrate deployability and collect indicative costs, but it should not claim a production SLA, certified security posture, legal interoperability, profitability or market traction without corresponding evidence.
chapter_one_integration.scope_inclusions: Include ZCDRRMO personnel and selected organization representatives as prototype users; customer-organization administrators; the workflow from report creation through review, correction, approval status and SitRep export; organization and role records; reference catalogs; dashboards linked to underlying records; onboarding, training, support and administrator-handover procedures; a documented hosting assumption; backup and export demonstrations; and an indicative lifecycle-cost worksheet. For startup feasibility, include stakeholder/problem interviews, evidence of the current workflow and cost, identification of the paying/contracting authority, procurement pathway mapping, minimum supplier documents, support responsibilities, proposed pricing basis, and a portability/termination concept. Distinguish end user, beneficiary, end-user unit, BAC/procurement actors, HoPE, budget/accounting/audit actors, data controller, and vendor because they make different decisions. Include dependencies on connectivity, customer devices, official forms, organization-supplied data, authorized reviewers, lawful data-sharing, and external government systems not controlled by the startup.
chapter_one_integration.limitations_and_delimitations: The prototype does not itself confer government authority, declare incidents, validate truth, replace emergency channels, dispatch responders, predict hazards, guarantee response-time reduction, or automatically submit an official SitRep. It is not evidence of DICT accreditation, PhilGEPS eligibility, procurement award, agency-wide adoption, cybersecurity certification, production availability, disaster resilience, profitability or willingness to pay. It does not integrate with national or local systems unless an implemented and tested interface is named. Evaluation is delimited to the participating organizations, roles, scenarios, devices, network conditions and study period. Prototype cost estimates exclude unknown future integrations, compliance work, procurement transaction cost, taxes, insurance, round-the-clock support, breach response and scale unless explicitly measured. Customer data remain subject to the responsible government's authority; startup access must be contractually limited. Expansion to other LGUs, hazards and public-safety decisions is outside the inference boundary until replicated under their mandates and workflows.
significance_causal_chains: For reporters: structured fields and draft recovery may produce more complete, traceable submissions, which may reduce avoidable clarification during review if users are trained, fields fit actual practice and connectivity recovery works. Possible harms are extra data-entry burden, false precision and exposure of sensitive data; compare completeness, corrections and task time against the current method.

For verifiers and SitRep staff: explicit states, attribution and source-linked exports may make review and compilation easier to audit, which may improve coordination if responsibilities and approval rules are formally assigned. Possible harms are automation bias and premature reliance on unverified entries; test source traceability, error detection, correction handling and reviewer agreement.

For ZCDRRMO management: dashboards may make the currently encoded records easier to summarize, which may support situational awareness if coverage is sufficiently complete and delays are visible. A dashboard cannot establish ground truth; measure latency, missingness, drill-down success and decisions made with versus without the prototype.

For participating organizations: tenant-specific administration may make onboarding and accountability clearer if an active administrator, training and turnover handover exist. Possible harms include abandoned accounts, excess privilege and cross-organization leakage; test offboarding, role review and isolation.

For the LGU as potential customer: a supported hosted service may shift some maintenance work to the startup and provide predictable service if procurement, budget, security, support and exit terms are viable. It may also create recurring cost and provider dependency; compare full lifecycle cost, service levels, migration effort and alternatives rather than acquisition price alone.

For the startup: pilot evidence may clarify product-market and workflow fit and improve a procurement-ready offer. It does not prove a scalable market; require multiple independent customer discoveries, a qualified opportunity, credible unit economics, support capacity and preferably paid or formally budgeted demand before making commercial claims.

safe_claims: RA 12254 provides a policy basis for government technology adoption, startup support and private-sector cooperation, while any contract remains subject to public-accountability and procurement rules.
The study evaluates a prototype and the conditions for organizational and commercial feasibility; it does not establish production readiness or procurement entitlement.
Usability and behavioral intention describe user acceptance under the tested conditions and are reported separately from willingness to pay, budget availability and procurement readiness.
Lifecycle feasibility includes acquisition, hosting, operation, maintenance, training, support, migration and exit costs, consistent with RA 12009's lifecycle orientation.
Observed improvements are limited to the measured tasks, users, data and conditions and are compared with a stated baseline.
claims_to_avoid: The E-Governance Act authorizes or guarantees adoption of the startup.
Positive SUS, UTAUT or interview responses prove that the LGU will pay for or procure the service.
The system ensures accurate reports, faster disaster response, public safety, transparency or resilience without an operational causal test.
A successful prototype is market-ready, scalable, secure, compliant or profitable.
ZCDRRMO results represent all Philippine LGUs or all disaster contexts.

authority_and_responsibility_matrix.responsibility: Create and amend reports within granted access; identify source and uncertainty; cannot approve or transform an entry into an official finding.
Assess evidence, record decision and rationale, request correction and flag conflicts under authority assigned by the customer; not authority created by the startup.
Approve SitRep content and perform any official transmission; remains accountable for official use.
Invite, disable and review users and roles for the organization, maintain local reference data and initiate handover; cannot access another customer's records.
Determine lawful purpose, classification, access, sharing, retention, disclosure, archival and disposition; approve incident-response and data-subject procedures.
Define need and functional requirements, conduct market scoping, prepare PPMP inputs, accept deliverables and monitor outcomes.
Perform the statutory procurement, authorization, funding, award, payment, accountability and audit functions; product users cannot substitute for them.

Operate only within contract and instructions; secure and support the service; disclose subprocessors/subcontractors; meet service, backup, breach, export, return/deletion and transition obligations; preserve logs and evidence.

Perform disclosed contracted functions under equivalent controls; RA 12009 requires applicable disclosure, eligibility and approval, while the prime remains liable for subcontractor defaults, delays and negligence.

system_and_governance.workflow_lineage_and_data_lifecycle: Use explicit Draft, Submitted, Under Review, Returned for Correction, Verified/Rejected, Approved for SitRep, Superseded and Archived states. Preserve creator, source organization, event and entry timestamps, location precision, attachments, stated uncertainty, verification actor/time/rationale, conflicts, corrections, approval and export identifiers. Never overwrite material history: create versions, link corrections and supersession, and show current versus prior status. Assign stable identifiers to reports and generated SitReps, and make each output traceable to the included report versions. Before deployment, the government authority must set classification, access, retention, archival, legal-hold, public-disclosure and disposition rules. Contract and tests should cover export in documented, machine-readable and human-readable formats; backup restoration; administrator handover; termination assistance; return of government data; deletion and deletion evidence for provider copies subject to lawful retention; and treatment of logs, backups and subcontractor copies.

module_specific_requirements.User and Organization Management: Customer-scoped tenants; least-privilege roles; unique accounts; invite, disable and transfer-administrator flows; periodic access review; authentication and audit logs; no cross-tenant lookup; documented support impersonation controls.
module_specific_requirements.Disaster Reporting: Required and optional fields aligned with actual forms; save-as-draft; validation; source and uncertainty capture; attachment limits; timestamp and location provenance; retry without duplicate creation; visible connectivity and submission status.
module_specific_requirements.Verification: Authorized queue; source view; decision states; reason and reviewer attribution; return-for-correction; conflict and duplicate handling; immutable history; no silent automatic verification.
module_specific_requirements.SitRep Generation: Select only eligible report versions; retain source links; display generation time, coverage and unresolved limitations; editable draft or export for authorized approval; version and approval record; no claim of automatic official submission.
module_specific_requirements.Catalog: Authorized maintenance of organizations, hazards, locations, status terms and other controlled values; effective dates; deactivation rather than destructive deletion; change history; import/export and validation.
module_specific_requirements.Dashboard: Role-scoped aggregates; filter definitions; data freshness, denominator and missing-data indicators; drill-down to permitted source records; accessible non-color cues; no predictive or causal label unless separately validated.

system_and_governance.risk_controls_and_residual_limits: Control privacy and re-identification through data minimization, role and tenant isolation, encryption, secure secrets, limited support access, logging, retention enforcement, tested deletion and privacy-by-design review. Control provider and subcontractor risk through disclosure, flow-down duties, incident notification, audit evidence, service levels, backups, recovery tests, financial/continuity review and termination assistance. Control connectivity risk with drafts, retry/idempotency, explicit sync state and tested low-bandwidth scenarios; a web prototype still cannot guarantee availability during infrastructure failure. Control accessibility with keyboard operation, labels, focus visibility, error identification, contrast and assistive-technology testing. Control automation bias by exposing sources, verification state, missingness and uncertainty and requiring authorized human approval. Residual risks remain from compromised customer devices, inaccurate source reports, insider misuse, correlated infrastructure outages, zero-day vulnerabilities, provider failure and organizational nonuse; the paper should state rather than promise away these risks.

metrics_comparators_and_test_conditions: Task completion rate = participants completing the defined task without critical error / participants attempting it; compare prototype with the documented current workflow for the same scenario.
Report-field completeness = applicable required fields correctly populated / applicable required fields; separately count incorrect, unknown and not-applicable entries.
Verification accuracy = correctly classified seeded cases / all seeded cases, with sensitivity and specificity where binary; use a domain-approved answer key and report reviewer disagreement.
SitRep traceability = sampled output assertions correctly linked to their source report version / sampled assertions; critical target should be 100%, with sample and sampling method reported.
Time on task runs from scenario start to accepted completion; report median and spread, failures separately, and whether network delay is included.
Usability may use SUS with scoring and respondent count reported; do not relabel it as effectiveness, willingness to pay or market demand.

Acceptance should separately measure performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, behavioral intention and observed use with a validated instrument where feasible.

Commercial discovery should record role, authority, current alternative and cost, problem severity, budget owner, procurement stage, target timing and evidence such as an approved plan, funded line, formal request or paid transaction. Do not count compliments or hypothetical interest as sales.

Run named scenarios on the actual supported phone and desktop classes, browsers, accessibility configuration and representative record volume under normal, throttled and interrupted connectivity. Thresholds require operational rationale or baseline evidence, not round numbers chosen after results.
evaluation_and_feasibility.adoption_cost_and_service_dependencies: Adoption depends on workflow fit, management sponsorship, assigned report/review/approval roles, initial and refresher training, protected staff time, turnover handover, customer administration, connectivity and devices, support channels, incident escalation and periodic access/data-quality review. A viability worksheet should separate one-time discovery, configuration, migration, integration, training and procurement costs from recurring hosting, storage, backups, monitoring, security maintenance, support, third-party services, taxes and compliance; include usage growth, after-hours coverage, breach/restore events and termination/migration. Define measurable availability and support windows, severity and response/restoration targets, maintenance notice, backup frequency, recovery tests, data location, subprocessor changes, security evidence, service credits/remedies, data export, deletion and transition assistance. Startup procurement readiness requires a legally registered and eligible supplier, required tax/licensing and PhilGEPS documents, financial and technical capacity, disclosed beneficial ownership/subcontractors, a bid/contract-ready service description, pricing, risk allocation and evidence proportionate to the mode. Market evidence should be graded: user intention < documented problem and buyer authority < qualified opportunity and budget pathway < pilot/MOU < paid pilot or award < renewal and multi-customer retention. Willingness to use is therefore not willingness to pay; the payer may be an LGU authority who does not operate the system. RA 12009 requires market scoping and permits fit-for-purpose modes, but the procuring entity—not the startup—selects and justifies the lawful route.
evaluation_and_feasibility.generalization_and_future_evidence: Current evidence covers only the prototype, participating ZCDRRMO-related users and organizations, chosen hazards, seeded or study-period data, devices and network conditions actually tested. Production claims require an independent security and privacy assessment, restore and recovery exercises, load/capacity evidence, accessibility testing, incident and continuity procedures, authoritative records/data-sharing decisions, and a time-bounded operational pilot with measured data quality, adoption, support burden and adverse events. Procurement claims require confirmation under the then-current RA 12009 rules, approved plan and budget, supplier eligibility and a completed lawful award process. Economic claims require fully loaded unit economics, customer-acquisition and procurement cost, support cost, churn/renewal, cash-cycle and concentration risk. Market generalization requires repeated buyer discovery and preferably paid deployments across multiple independent LGUs or comparable organizations; policy or public-safety benefit requires comparative longitudinal evidence and analysis of alternative explanations. Replicate by hazard, organizational maturity, urban/rural setting, connectivity, deployment size and user role before presenting national applicability.
